case.description: Design a removable joint for a 300 mm inspection hatch on a dry tabletop trough fixture. A technician must open it repeatedly while retaining the existing hatch, rim and seal. All dimensions and observations below are stipulated for this hypothetical fixture.
case.valued_outcome: After ten opening cycles, the closed hatch stays within 1 mm of its marked position, withstands a supplied 20 N sideways pull, and can be reopened by one technician within 30 seconds.
hard_constraints: Do not drill, cut, glue or permanently deform the hatch or trough.
Keep the full marked inspection opening unobstructed when open.
Use no powered mechanism; loose components must remain recoverable.
The seal must show no new visible tears after testing.
resources: One 300 by 180 mm hatch, one trough rim and one 2 mm removable seal.
Four 100 by 25 by 3 mm aluminum strips, two 250 mm fabric straps, six M4 bolts with nuts, four rubber pads and 1 m of cord.
One hand drill usable only on supplied strips, one hacksaw, two spanners, ruler and marker.
Ninety minutes for fabrication and twenty minutes for observation.
observations: The untreated hatch slides 4 mm under the 20 N pull.
The seal leaves a continuous contact mark when the hatch is centered.
Awkward observation: pressing the hatch more tightly at its left corner makes the opposite corner lift 2 mm; this occurred in three supplied trials.

openings.claim: Extra downward corner compression is supposedly necessary for lateral retention. A possible counterexample transfers sideways load through removable edge stops while removing that extra compression; neither retention implies tight compression nor tight compression implies retention.
openings.delta: Use the four strips as two bolted, rubber-protected rim clips, with removable keeper portions beside and above opposite hatch edges. Adjust clearance without forcing the left corner downward. Slide both clips completely clear for opening; tether recoverable components with cord. The changed dependency is lateral edge bearing instead of added seal friction from corner pressure.
openings.prediction: Nearest rival: the same clips retain the hatch mainly because downward preload increases seal friction. Edge-bearing restraint predicts at most 1 mm displacement under 20 N with light preload and no induced opposite-corner lift. The friction rival predicts deterioration when extra preload is removed. These are prospective observations, not established performance.
openings.probe: First check whether supplied strips can capture the existing rim and hatch without modification. Within ninety minutes fabricate only if that geometry permits. Allocate twelve closure/pull trials: two ordinary tightened closures, one with the right-contact card; then ten removal-arm opening cycles, final closure disturbed. Measure marked-position deviation, apply the supplied 20 N scale pull, time reopening by one technician, and inspect seal tears each cycle. Observe corner lift as a discriminating mechanism measurement. Fit all observations within twenty minutes.
assumptions: Rim underside access, hatch-edge clearance and keeper removal paths are unspecified; inaccessible geometry defeats this construction.
Pads and strip contact can protect the hatch, rim and seal without permanent deformation; this requires inspection.
Clip grip and strip stiffness must transmit 20 N without slip or excessive bending; supplied dimensions do not establish capacity.

Reject the counterexample if any candidate cycle exceeds 1 mm displacement or thirty seconds reopening, produces a new tear, obstructs the opened inspection area, or fails the disturbed closure. Stop before damage if tightening threatens a hard constraint; an incomplete probe establishes no outcome.

artifact.assessment: One tentative removal operation. Geometry and capacity remain indispensable unknowns, so no feasible counterexample or deployment is demonstrated. Avoiding extra compression alone does not establish seal stability.

openings.claim: A removable lateral stop joint may resist sliding without the corner compression associated with opposite-corner lift.
openings.delta: Change the load carrier from seal friction under downward preload to hatch edges bearing against supplied-strip stops. Cut and drill only the strips; use bolted, rubber-padded removable rim clamps to support the stops, with vertical release clearance. Nearest rival: a padded hold-down joint relying on friction.
openings.prediction: With adequate clamp purchase and stop stiffness, edge restraint should limit displacement without tightening the left corner. The rival predicts that reducing preload restores sliding, while raising preload can reproduce opposite-corner lift. Equivalent displacement and lift across configurations would not discriminate; stop slip or opposite-corner lift defeats the proposed separation of lateral restraint from compression.
openings.probe: First use ruler inspection to establish accessible rim purchase, bolt reach and a stop arrangement locating the marked position while permitting full hatch removal. If these are absent, park the design. Fabricate at most two configurations: edge restraint and padded hold-down. Give each ten opening cycles; measure closure position, reopening time and new seal tears. Perform pulls after cycles one and ten, then one additional closure/pull with the stipulated right-contact card per configuration: six total trials. Record displacement and opposite-corner lift before and during each 20 N pull. Remove or relocate every rim component outside the full marked opening during opening; retain recoverability with the supplied cord. Stop fabrication if the ninety-minute allowance cannot accommodate both configurations.
assumptions: Rim geometry permits removable clamps and unobstructed release; this is unprovided.
Supplied strips, six bolts and pads can form sufficiently stiff stops without altering hatch or trough.
Cord routing and the twenty-minute observation allowance permit the stated cycles and measurements; verify rather than assume.
Seal protection must be checked after each cycle; visible tearing fails the hard constraint.

artifact.assessment: One speculative opening. It preserves the intended outcome but feasibility remains unresolved because rim attachment geometry and carrier capacity are unspecified. The dimensional check is a resource gate, not performance evidence; the cycle/pull comparison is a probe, not deployment.

openings.claim: Transfer sideways restraint from seal friction to removable locating bolts carried by two padded strip saddles. A separate, balanced hold-down setting may avoid the observed opposite-corner lift. Neither attachment capacity nor success is supplied.
openings.delta: Drill only strips; bolt them as two upper/lower rim saddles using four bolts and four pads. Use the remaining bolts as hatch-edge locators along the pull direction; tether recoverable parts with cord. Release and move saddles entirely outside the marked opening. Nearest rival: straps increasing normal force and relying on seal friction.
openings.prediction: Locators predict less sideways displacement without increased corner compression; the friction rival predicts restraint changing with compression. Defeat: saddles move, locator clearance exceeds 1 mm, disturbed closure rocks, reopening exceeds 30 seconds, or seal damage appears. Locating along the pull direction alone does not establish repeatability in the other direction.
openings.probe: Confirm accessible rim underside, locator reach, reversible pad seating and full open clearance before fabrication. Within twelve closure/pull trials, run ten candidate cycles, including a disturbed final closure; measure position, 20 N displacement, reopening time and visible seal condition. Reserve two disturbed trials for the feedback comparison, with equal initial closure setting and 20 N demand. A comparison counts only if the stated return response can be varied safely and measurably.
assumptions: Rim access, strip/bolt geometry, cord anchorage and clamp capacity are indispensable unknowns; supplied strips may not form these saddles within ninety minutes.

Hypothesized arrows: friction-dependent restraint mechanism → demand for extra compression after slip; demand → technician left-corner tightening response; response → mechanism through opposite-corner lift and reduced contact. Only tightening → lift is supplied; the other arrows and friction effect remain hypotheses.

Remove slip-triggered extra tightening without removing inspection access or restraint, using preset balanced closure. Sham retains that return rule with identical initial demand. No return influence: displacement and corner lift do not differ beyond ruler resolution. Invalid sham execution leaves the loop unresolved.

artifact.assessment: Bounded feasibility and discrimination probe; unknown geometry prevents a deployment claim. Ten-cycle success must satisfy every stated outcome, including disturbed position, pull resistance and reopening.

openings.claim: Explore reversible positive lateral registration with balanced retention. Lateral load would travel through hatch-edge stops into removable rim anchors; straps would supply only separation restraint.
openings.delta: Use the four strips as two opposed, pad-protected bolted anchor assemblies, if actual rim geometry permits. Locate stop hardware against hatch edges without penetrating either original part. Route the two straps across the 180 mm direction with balanced tension. Tether removable hardware using the supplied cord and remove assemblies clear of the marked opening during access.
openings.prediction: Compared with balanced friction-only retention, positive bearing should make sideways displacement less sensitive to reduced seal pressure. The right-side card may still provoke rocking: bearing does not establish acceptable seating, seal survival or reopening time.
openings.probe: First make an untensioned dimensional mock-up: verify opposed bearing contacts, accessible reversible anchoring, 250 mm strap reach, hardware recovery and full opening clearance. Reject fabrication if any requires forbidden alteration or extra resources. If feasible, drill only strips and use at most two preliminary closure/pull trials to check seating. Then perform ten opening/closure/pull trials, with the supplied card at the right contact on the final closure. Measure marked-position error and 20 N displacement, time one-technician reopening, and inspect the seal after every cycle. Stop on new tears or unstable hardware; stopping is not a passing result.
assumptions: Rim profile and underside access admit bolted strip anchors; these dimensions are unprovided.
Existing bolts can form effective hatch-edge bearing contacts without passing through original material.
Strap reach, cord length, ninety-minute fabrication and twenty-minute observation capacity suffice; verify rather than assume.

artifact.assessment: This is a fabrication-gated probe, not deployment. Acceptance requires all stipulated outcomes: within 1 mm after ten cycles, withstand 20 N, reopen within 30 seconds, unobstructed access, recoverable components and no new visible seal tears. Inaccessible anchoring, inadequate strap reach, excessive rocking or failed timing defeats this proposal. The supplied corner-lift observation motivates balanced loading but does not prove its cause.
